headline: Lorient beat Monaco and arrive at Angers as favourites
summary: Lorient beat league leaders Monaco 1-0 on matchday 7 and arrive at Angers as the market's favourites. Angers are 15th on 7 points and have conceded five goals in each of their last two matches — 2-5 at home to Marseille, then 1-5 at Brest. Midfielder Haris Belkebla is still out of training, Ouest-France report. With the margin removed, Lorient are 39.3% to win against Angers' 31.6%, and their price has fallen from 2.81 to 2.46. The handicap gives Angers a quarter-goal start. Against that, Angers won this fixture 2-0 last October.
read: In recent days the market has turned this into a Lorient match: they are 39.3% favourites against Angers' 31.6%, and the handicap has moved from level to a shade in their favour. The football lines up — Lorient beat league leaders Monaco 1-0 last weekend, while Angers have conceded five goals in each of their last two games.

facts.fact: Lorient are the market's favourites at 39.3% to win at Angers, with the home side on 31.6%.
facts.meaning: The away team is the more likely winner, though the market still rates this as a close match rather than a one-sided one.

facts.fact: Angers have conceded five goals in each of their last two matches — 2-5 at home to Marseille and 1-5 at Brest.
facts.meaning: It is the run that turned the market against them, and it is the biggest single question hanging over the home side here.

facts.fact: Lorient beat league leaders Monaco 1-0 on matchday 7 — Monaco's first defeat of the season.
facts.meaning: They arrive as the form side and as the market's favourites, which is why the away price keeps shortening.

facts.fact: Angers are 15th in Ligue 1 with seven points from seven matches, while Lorient are seventh on 11.
The handicap fair line has moved from -0.05 to +0.15, so Angers now get a quarter-goal start and the market rates Lorient the better side even away from home.
facts.meaning: A fixture the market first rated level is now a shade in Lorient's favour — a full fifth of a goal of movement.

facts.fact: Haris Belkebla, who missed the Marseille defeat, is still absent from Angers training four days before kick-off.
facts.meaning: Angers are short in midfield again for the visit of the side sitting seventh — background: Belkebla is normally a central midfielder.

facts.fact: Alexandre Dujeux, now Lorient's coach, returns to Angers, the club he used to manage.
The market's goals line sits at 2.4 and Over 2.5 is priced at 47.2% — a slight lean toward under three goals.
facts.meaning: Despite 13 goals in Angers' last two matches, the market expects a tighter game than those scorelines suggest.

sources.fact: Angers have conceded ten goals in their last two matches, including a 2-5 home defeat to Marseille.
Angers lost 2-5 at home to Marseille in Ligue 1 on matchday 7.
Haris Belkebla, who missed the Marseille match through injury, is still absent from Angers training four days before facing Lorient.
Ousmane Camara, who was absent against Marseille, has returned to training with the Angers squad.
Emmanuel Biumla is training away from the Angers first-team group and is doubtful to face Lorient.
Angers sit on 7 points after seven matches and view the visit of Lorient as an immediate chance to respond after the Marseille defeat.
Lorient beat Monaco 1-0 on matchday 7, handing the leaders their first defeat of the season.
Alexandre Dujeux, Lorient's current coach, is Angers' former coach and will face his old club.
